met_analysis:
The Well Marked Low Pressure Area over Eastcentral and adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal persisted over the same region at 1430 hours IST of today, the 24th October, 2026. The associated cyclonic circulation extends upto 7.6 km above mean sea level. It is most likely to persist over the same region and intensify into a depression today, the 24th October, 2026. Thereafter, it is very likely to move west-northwestwards and intensify further into a deep depression on 25th October & into a cyclonic storm over the Westcentral Bay of Bengal by 26th October morning. Moving west-northwestwards, it would continue to intensify further and reach over Westcentral Bay of Bengal near Andhra Pradesh coast around morning of 28th October, 2026.
The Low Pressure areaover Southeast Arabian sea and adjoining Lakshadweep area persisted over the same region at 1430 hrs IST of today, the 24th October, 2026. The associated cyclonic circulation extends upto 7.6 km above mean sea level.
The trough from the cyclonic circulation associated with Low Pressure areaover Southeast Arabian sea and adjoining Lakshadweep to north coastal Tamilnadu across Kerala extending upto 1.5 km above mean sea level persists. Theupper air cyclonic circulation over northeast Bangladesh & neighbourhood extending upto 1.5 km above mean sea level persists.
The Western Disturbance as a cyclonic circulation over north Pakistan & neighbourhood between 3.1 & 5.8 km above mean sea level persists with the trough aloft in upper tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 7.6 km above mean sea level now runs roughly along Long. 72°E to the north of Lat. 30°N.
The induced upper cyclonic circulation over West Rajasthan & neighbourhood extending upto 1.5 km above mean sea level persists.
